title: Cancer-associated fusion transcripts: mechanisms, functional roles, and clinical implications.
one_liner_zh: 综述癌症融合转录本的形成机制、功能与临床意义，虽提及AI辅助计算但未聚焦蛋白质-DNA互作或TF-DNA结合建模，与本课题关联薄弱。
abstract: Fusion transcripts are hybrid RNA molecules generated through genomic rearrangements or RNA-level fusion mechanisms. They represent important molecular features of many cancers and can function as oncogenic drivers, diagnostic biomarkers, prognostic indicators, and therapeutic targets. Since the discovery of the BCR::ABL1 fusion in chronic myeloid leukemia, numerous cancer-associated fusion transcripts have been identified across hematologic malignancies and solid tumors. These fusion events encompass diverse biological mechanisms, including constitutively active kinases, aberrant transcription factors, epigenetic regulators, and non-coding fusion RNAs. This review summarizes current knowledge of the mechanisms underlying fusion transcript formation, including genomic rearrangement-dependent and rearrangement-independent processes, as well as fusion circular RNAs. The functional roles of fusion transcripts in cancer biology and their clinical relevance as diagnostic, prognostic, and predictive biomarkers are discussed. In addition, recent advances in fusion transcript detection and characterization are reviewed, including next-generation sequencing, long-read sequencing, single-cell approaches, artificial intelligence-assisted computational methods, and CRISPR/Cas9-mediated strategies for functional modeling and functional validation of fusion transcripts. Despite the rapid expansion of fusion transcript catalogs, the biological and clinical significance of most identified fusion events remains incompletely understood. Future progress will depend on integrating advanced sequencing technologies, artificial intelligence-assisted computational prioritization, and systematic functional validation to distinguish clinically actionable fusion transcripts from biologically neutral events. Such multidisciplinary approaches will be essential for translating fusion transcript research into precision oncology and improving cancer diagnosis, patient stratification, and targeted therapy.
abstract_zh: 融合转录本是通过基因组重排或RNA水平融合机制产生的杂交RNA分子。它们代表了许多癌症的重要分子特征，可作为致癌驱动因子、诊断生物标志物、预后指标和治疗靶点。自从在慢性髓性白血病中发现BCR::ABL1融合以来，在血液系统恶性肿瘤和实体瘤中已鉴定出大量与癌症相关的融合转录本。这些融合事件涵盖多种生物学机制，包括组成性激活的激酶、异常转录因子、表观遗传调控因子和非编码融合RNA。本综述总结了目前关于融合转录本形成机制的知识，包括依赖基因组重排和不依赖重排的过程，以及融合环状RNA。讨论了融合转录本在癌症生物学中的功能作用及其作为诊断、预后和预测性生物标志物的临床相关性。此外，综述了融合转录本检测和表征的最新进展，包括下一代测序、长读长测序、单细胞方法、人工智能辅助计算方法和CRISPR/Cas9介导的融合转录本功能建模与功能验证策略。尽管融合转录本目录迅速扩展，但大多数已鉴定融合事件的生物学和临床意义仍未完全阐明。未来的进展将依赖于整合先进测序技术、人工智能辅助计算优先级排序和系统性功能验证，以区分具有临床可操作性的融合转录本与生物学中性事件。这种多学科方法对于将融合转录本研究转化为精准肿瘤学以及改善癌症诊断、患者分层和靶向治疗至关重要。
